cause.classification: Vendor detector state leaks a parser-specific cookie across build-file contexts during GLOBAL dependency analysis.
facts: GradleDetector stores agpVersionCheckInfo.cookie without its originating Context.
In32.0.1 the field appears only at declaration183, assignment1253, and reuse2156: it is never cleared.
afterCheckFile(context) reuses that saved cookie with the current file Context.
LintDriver chooses UastGradleVisitor for .gradle.kts, GroovyGradleVisitor for .gradle; the latter unconditionally casts the supplied cookie to Groovy ASTNode.
The observed cookie is a Kotlin UAST node while the current visitor is Groovy, matching this exact failure mechanism.
The crash occurs during analyzeLibraryProject/analyzeDependencies, with75 complete models; no source evidence indicates a BIL app runtime failure or a duplicate-classloader cast.
cause.notProven: The log does not identify the exact originating KTS file and succeeding Groovy file. Do not invent their names.

processLifecycle.observedByRoot: Child PID6068 had exited main/DestroyJavaVM and AWT shutdown remained, delaying Gradle after the fatal exception. Root owns process termination and current --continue run.
processLifecycle.proposedTaskTimeout: JavaExec Task.timeout 30minutes for the analysis phase only, after model dependencies. This is a proposed operational bound, not a measured performance guarantee.
processLifecycle.behavior: Call unchanged official Main.run with all original arguments, retain its returned exit code, and System.exit(nonzero) after uncaught Throwable with full raw stack. This fixes termination reporting only; it does not fix or hide the vendor detector crash.

Use the headless/bounded exit wrapper only in a new, separately fingerprinted audit-tool run after validating normal/nonzero/uncaught-failure exits.
